Only methods declared in candy-git/src, or inherited from a parent declared there, are listed. A type that extends a class outside that tree, such as \RuntimeException, does not show the methods of that class.

SugarCraft\Git

App final class

Three-pane git TUI: status (left), branches (top right), log (bottom right). Tab cycles focus; up/down moves the cursor in the active pane; s stages / unstages the highlighted status entry; a stages all files; Space (branches pane) checks out the selected branch; c opens inline commit message collection; ? shows the help overlay; R refreshes from disk. u / Ctrl+r for undo/redo. f / p / P fetch, pull and push the tracked remote (each behind the same armed confirm as the destructive verbs).

static start(GitDriver $git): self
init(): ?\Closure
update(Msg $msg): array
view(): string
paneWidth(): intWidth of each of the two side-by-side pane columns. Derived from the terminal width reported via WindowSizeMsg — the two columns split the width minus the border/padding/gutter overhead — and falls back to the historical constant until a size arrives so first-frame output stays byte-stable.
listRows(): ?intRows available for the pane/overlay area after fixed chrome (header row, help line, trailing row) and any notice or prompt bars. null until the terminal reports its size — callers then treat lists as unbounded, which is the historical byte-stable first-frame output (the height was stored but never read, so every list and overlay rendered in full and appended below each other off the bottom of the screen).
hintRows(): intRows the key-hint strip gets (candy-git-032). The monolithic sentence put the rarest verbs first, so q and ? — the two affordances the strip exists for — never survived truncation at any realistic width. The contextual rebuild uses a second row when the screen can pay it (>= 16 rows: a laptop frame still has six pane rows); short frames keep one row, and essentials-first ordering guarantees that row ends with the verbs the pane actually answers to, not with 'quit'.
overlayOpen(): boolWhether a full overlay is open and must share the screen with the lists.
rightColumnBodyRows(): intBody rows shared by the right-column pair after both frames pay their two border rows. The pair used to floor independently at 1 each, so the stack demanded branches(3)+log(3)=6 rows from a 5-row area on an h=8 terminal — the log body vanished behind the hard ceiling while the frame still claimed it was rendered (candy-git-033). Deriving the budget from the enforced minimums keeps demand ≤ supply at every height: a pane appears only when its borders plus one body row fit.
statusBodyRows(): intVisible status-list rows (frame borders excluded; 0 = no room for the pane).
branchesBodyRows(): intVisible branch-list rows: the right column stacks branches over log.
logBodyRows(): intVisible log rows: the right-column remainder below branches.
overlayBodyRows(): intRows an open overlay gets; a tiny floor so short screens still show a frame.
cursorTarget(): ?stringThe plain-text cursor modeline: what the keyboard currently acts on.
barWidth(): intHorizontal budget for full-width prompt/notice bars.
statusPathWidth(): intStatus-pane path budget: pane width minus padding (2) and the 3-col "XY " marker.
branchNameWidth(): intBranch-name budget: pane width minus padding (2) and the 2-col current-branch marker.
logSubjectWidth(): intLog-subject budget: pane width minus padding (2) and the short-sha + 2-space gap (8).
isTyping(): boolWhether a text-collection buffer currently owns the keyboard: in these states printable keys belong to the buffer, and global quit keys that collide with letters (q) must not fire. Escape/Ctrl+C still cancel via the global chain — only the letter collision is gated.
refresh(): self
subscriptions(): ?\SugarCraft\Core\Subscriptions

Git final class

Thin wrapper around git invocations. Everything that mutates a repo shells out — no libgit2 binding, no in-PHP plumbing-command reimplementation. The wrapper is split out so tests can swap in a fixture-backed Git (or its parent interface, GitDriver) without touching the runtime.

static isBareRepository(string $cwd): boolBare repos answer rev-parse --is-bare-repository with true. They have no work tree, so every status-pane verb (stage, discard, stash) is meaningless here — the launcher refuses one instead of booting a TUI whose whole first pane would error.

True when commit.gpgsign resolves true and gpg.format is not ssh: SSH-format signing rides the ssh-agent socket the user already unlocked, while classic GPG prompts on /dev/tty - an input channel candy-git's stdin isolation cannot fence (candy-git-054). Exit-code probes, never run(): "key not set" is the common case.

conflictedPathsCarryingMarkers(): arrayPaths git still reports as unmerged whose FILE BYTES carry conflict markers. git add -A is marker-blind (it stages whatever is on disk, candy-git-090) - so staging-all during a conflicted merge can commit the literal <<<<<<< machinery as resolved content. The App arms a named confirm for exactly this list.
localHooksPresent(): boolDoes this repository ship live hooks that git will run for us? .git/hooks is not cloned, but a supplied or dev-image repo can carry executable hooks, and every other repo-controlled execution channel candy-git either disarms or announces (candy-git-144) - hooks ride the all-verbs posture, so they get the same honesty: probe here, announce in-app, document in the trust boundary. Linked worktrees share the MAIN git dir, which is where the live hooks actually sit.

Plain git diff emits nothing for ?? rows, so the routine "what is this new file" action opened an empty box (candy-git-035). The shape is git's own new-file patch (byte-verified against git diff --no-index -- /dev/null <path>), built from a file read - not a spawn - so hosts without /dev/null are unaffected and the spawn census does not move.

GitDriver interface

Pluggable git backend. Production is Git (shells out to the git binary). Tests inject a fixture closure-driven implementation so transition correctness can be asserted without staging real repos in tmp dirs.

MethodSummary
status(): arrayParse git status --porcelain=v1 -b.
branches(): array
log(int $limit = 25): array

unstage(string $path): void
checkout(string $branch): void

commit(string $message): void

diff(string $path, bool $cached = false): array
discard(string $path): voidDiscard working-tree changes for a file (git restore --worktree <path>).
untrackedDiff(string $path): arrayThe all-additions diff of an untracked path (candy-git-035: a plain diff is empty for ?? rows, so the review action opened a blank box). Read from the file, never spawned.
deleteUntracked(string $path): voidRemove an untracked file from disk - the armed d on a ?? row. git restore cannot touch untracked paths, so this is a true, unrecoverable unlink (candy-git-035).
amend(): voidAmend the last commit without changing its message (--no-edit).
amendWith(string $message): voidRewrite the last commit with a new message (candy-git-013: the pre-filled amend collector submits through here).

commitGpgSigns(): boolWhether a commit here will be GPG-signed through gpg-agent's pinentry on /dev/tty (candy-git-054) — the commit collector's hint lane uses this to warn before the signing step can paint over the frame.
conflictedPathsCarryingMarkers(): arrayRepo-relative paths git still reports as unmerged whose file bytes carry conflict markers (candy-git-090) - the App arms a named confirm for staging all when this list is non-empty, because git add -A is marker-blind.
localHooksPresent(): boolWhether the repository ships executable hooks that our own commit verbs will run unannounced (candy-git-144) - the collector warns once per session when this is true.
stagePatch(string $path, string $hunk): voidStage a single hunk via git apply --cached.
unstageAll(): voidUnstage all staged changes (inverse of stageAll).
unstagePatch(string $path, string $hunk): voidUnstage a single hunk by applying the patch in reverse.
createBranch(string $name, ?string $from = null): voidCreate and switch to a new branch.
commitDetails(string $ref): arrayFull commit display — headers, message, stat summary and patch. Feeds the log pane's read-only details overlay (candy-git-015).
revert(string $ref): voidInvert a commit onto HEAD as a new commit (revert --no-edit).
resetHard(string $ref): voidMove HEAD to a ref and overwrite the worktree (reset --hard). Destructive by definition — the UI arms it.
deleteBranch(string $name): voidDelete a branch (safe, -d flag).
restoreBranch(string $name, string $sha): voidRestore a deleted branch pointing at a previously recorded sha.
merge(string $branch): voidMerge a branch into the current branch.
mergeAbort(): voidAbandon a stopped (conflicted) merge, restoring the pre-merge state.
mergeContinue(): voidCommit the resolution of a conflicted merge (continue leg).
fetch(): voidFetch from the default remote: updates tracking refs, never the worktree.
pull(): voidPull the tracked remote branch into the current one (merge back-end, non-interactive).
push(): voidPush the current branch. A branch without an upstream goes to origin with --set-upstream recorded; a detached HEAD has no branch to push and throws.
rebaseContinue(): voidContinue an in-progress rebase.
rebaseAbort(): voidAbort an in-progress rebase.
rebaseSkip(): voidSkip the current rebase commit.
reset(): voidReset HEAD to the parent of the last commit (undo last commit, keep changes staged).
stashList(): arrayList stashes (parse git stash list).
stashApply(string $stashRef): voidApply a stash by its ref (e.g. "stash@{0}").
stashDrop(string $stashRef): voidDrop (delete) a stash by its ref.
stashPush(?string $message, bool $keepIndex = false, bool $includeUntracked = false): voidCreate a stash from the current worktree/index (git stash push).
stashPop(string $stashRef): voidPop a stash: apply then drop (candy-git-014). Composed from the two guarded verbs rather than spawning git stash pop — a conflicted apply throws before the drop, so the entry survives for a retry, and the merge-capable dispatch guard already verifies the apply shape without needing a new argv lane in its tables.
stashSha(string $stashRef): stringResolve a stash ref to its commit sha (candy-git-120).
stashSubject(string $stashRef): stringRe-insert a dropped stash entry at the top of the stash list (candy-git-120).

cherryPick(string $commit): voidCherry-pick a commit.
cherryPickContinue(): voidContinue an in-progress cherry-pick.
cherryPickAbort(): voidAbort an in-progress cherry-pick.
worktreeList(): arrayList worktrees (parse git worktree list --porcelain).
worktreeAdd(string $path, string $branch): voidAdd a new worktree at $path. A non-empty $branch is CREATED from HEAD (-b); an empty one lets git name the branch from the path basename. Neither leg detaches (CG-24).
worktreeRemove(string $path): voidRemove an existing worktree at $path.
sequenceState(): stringSequencer stop state: 'rebase' | 'cherry' | 'merge' | '' (none).

InteractiveRebase final readonly class

Interactive rebase todo state — a READ-ONLY preview list built from the recent commits. Action cycling and dropping were preview theatre (candy-git-011): the todo is discarded on Esc and nothing is ever executed. Parked per gate G1 (2026-11-14): the App refuses the mutating keys with the preview-only notice; the model methods below stay as the building blocks for the wire arm (temp todo + GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR) should the owner commission it. Wiring it needs a GitDriver execution method and an Enter arm; the completion, error and cancel plumbing that anticipated them is deleted as speculation (candy-git-029 part 3).

Lang final class

Per-library translation facade for candy-git.

Pane enum

Which pane has focus. The Tab key cycles forward through them. Every pane carries the row cursor and viewport movement; the status pane is the one that takes file-line actions (stage/unstage/discard/diff) and the branches pane the one that takes branch actions (Space checkout, D delete, w worktrees overlay), while the log pane opens commit details and acts on the commit under the cursor (candy-git-015). Repo-wide verbs — commit, amend, new branch, merge, cherry-pick, rebase, undo/redo — dispatch regardless of which pane holds focus.

Cases: Status · Branches · Log

PHP also provides cases(), from() and tryFrom().

MethodSummary
next(): self

Platform final class

The OS seam under Process: every place the subprocess runner differs between POSIX and Windows is answered here, and nowhere else.

MethodSummary
static new(): selfThe host platform.
static posix(): self
static windows(): self
isWindows(): bool
nullDevice(): stringPath whose read end is an immediate EOF (the child's stdin when no payload is given).
withNullDevice(string $path): self
withKillTree(\Closure $killTree): self
findExecutable(string $name, ?string $path = null): ?stringResolves a program on PATH the way the OS would (PATHEXT suffixes on Windows), or null. Lets the CLI tell "git is not installed" apart from "git is installed but could not be launched".
resolveSpawnProgram(array $argv, ?string $path = null): arrayRewrite a bare argv[0] to its OS-resolved path, the way cmd.exe would. CreateProcess appends only .exe to a bare program name, so a git that ships as git.cmd - a shim, or a PATH wrapper - dies with error 2 at spawn time on the very hosts where it IS installed. Resolving through findExecutable walks the same PATHEXT family. Best-effort by contract: tokens that already spell a path, and names nothing resolves, are handed back untouched so spawnFailure's reason stays honest.
killTree(int $pid): voidForce-stop the process tree rooted at $pid (Windows ladder only).

Version final class

The version string this tool reports on --version.

MethodSummary
static line(): stringThe --version line: plain text, newline-terminated, produced by no state and no host probe — the flag must answer anywhere.
static current(): stringThe version this process reports: the archive stamp when running from a stamped phar, self::CURRENT everywhere else.
static fromPharMetadata(string $path): ?stringThe version a phar archive at $path was built to carry, or null when it names none (unreadable archive, wrong metadata shape, the dev-build sentinel, or an empty stamp). Every refusal is a null, never an exception — --version must answer on a machine whose phar cannot be opened.
static versionFromMetadata(mixed $metadata): ?stringThe judgement on the stamp itself, split out because the archive-open leg is unreachable from a suite that must not build phars: the release namespace strip, the dev-build refusal, and the wrong-type nulls are a pure function over what getMetadata() answers.
static hostArchive(): stringThe filesystem path of the phar this process was launched from, or '' when it was not launched from one — the two-identity law measured on candy-code's real builds and pinned by the bin autoload guard: inside archive-loaded code Phar::running(false) answers the archive path, while the stub context answers '' and there a '.phar'-suffixed __DIR__ is the enclosing archive.
